title: Mild phenotype in an adult male with X‐linked adrenoleukodystrophy – case report
case_prompt:
A 61-year-old Norwegian man was referred for evaluation of presumed Parkinson’s disease. He first noted frequent leg fasciculations at age 48. Neurophysiology at that time showed a mild sensorimotor peripheral neuropathy. At age 51, bilateral Babinski signs were present, and over the next decade he developed mild tetraspasticity, symmetrical hyperreflexia, muscle stiffness, gait difficulty, and unsteadiness, yet remained able to run and hike. At age 57, he developed asymmetric bradykinesia and rigidity. He had an excellent response to levodopa, returned to near-normal function, remained fully ambulatory, and worked full time. His father had levodopa-responsive Parkinson’s disease; there was no family history of myelopathy or adrenal disease. On examination, his Spastic Paraplegia Rating Scale score was 4/52 and his Expanded Disability Status Scale score was 3.0. 

Investigations at age 61 included:  
• CSF with normal cell count and protein, no oligoclonal bands  
• MRI of brain and spinal cord with no demyelination, Loes score 0  
• Brain DaTscan showing asymmetrically reduced basal ganglia uptake consistent with Parkinson’s disease  
• Electromyography and nerve conduction studies showing moderate predominantly axonal sensorimotor neuropathy of the lower extremities  
• Skin biopsy with reduced intraepidermal nerve-fiber density  
• Endocrine studies including cortisol and ACTH stimulation test within normal limits  
• Serum very long-chain fatty acids elevated (C26:0 1.02 mg/L; C26:0/C22:0 ratio 0.058)  
• ABCD1 gene sequencing demonstrating a previously unreported missense variant of uncertain significance
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy was considered because of accumulation of very long‐chain fatty acids — “Elevated levels of very long‐chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) had raised the possibility of X‐ALD as a differential diagnosis.”  
2. Parkinson’s disease was supported by imaging and treatment response — “Brain SPECT using DaTscan … consistent with PD” and “there was an excellent response to levodopa therapy.”  
3. Multisystem atrophy of the striatonigral form was excluded — “Multisystem atrophy of the striatonigral form … was unlikely, given the excellent response to levodopa therapy.”  
4. Cramps-fasciculation syndrome was excluded — “The patient did not fit with criteria for the cramps‐fasciculation syndrome …”  
5. Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis was excluded — “The patient did not fit with criteria … for … amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.”
